content.title: About
content.content: Fruit salad with citrus fruits and marshmallows is a mix of fresh oranges, grapefruits, lemons, limes, kiwi, berries and soft marshmallows, tossed in a light syrup. It combines the bright tang of citrus with the gentle sweetness of marshmallows, creating a refreshing dessert suitable for any season.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C, which supports immunity and aids iron absorption.
Marshmallows were originally created in ancient Egypt as a medicinal remedy for colds.
The contrast of sour and sweet flavors enhances aroma perception, making the salad more fragrant.
Fruit salad is often served at celebrations because its vivid colors create a festive atmosphere.
Citrus acidity helps slow down oxidation of other fruits, extending the salad’s freshness.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Citrus fruits provide an excellent source of vitamin C, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress and supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in citrus help combat free radicals, reducing the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the fruits improves bowel function and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides quick energy
items.content: Simple sugars in marshmallows and fruits quickly replenish glucose stores, giving an instant energy boost.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium in citrus helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to citrus, ranging from itching to swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Marshmallows add a significant amount of sugar, which may be undesirable for diabetics or those watching their weight.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some commercial marshmallows contain artificial flavors and preservatives that can cause sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled; you can add fresh mint or a light honey drizzle. It’s easy to eat with a spoon or fork, and it also works well as a topping for pancakes or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the fruit salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days. Marshmallows may soften, so it’s best to add them just before serving.
